task.brief: Investigate process_file at /process/file in this Open WebUI revision. Trace the caller, the supplied file_id and the destination collection_name through authorization and the eventual processing or vector write. Explain whether the object authorized for input and the object affected by output are the same, and what happens for caller-owned versus another user's file. Do not assume the caller owns the destination collection. Give visible conditions and specific remaining limits; this is behavior investigation.

behavior.explanation: The verified caller and supplied file_id are checked through an admin-versus-owner-constrained lookup. If a file is selected, collection_name is caller-supplied or derived from that file, and the selected file is processed and potentially written to that collection. No collection authorization check is visible.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

behavior.explanation: The endpoint binds the caller through Depends(get_verified_user), then authorizes selection of the supplied file_id by role: admins look up any file by ID, while non-admins use a lookup constrained by both file_id and user.id. If a file is selected, the destination is the supplied collection_name or the derived name file-{file.id}. The handler processes content and updates the selected file; unless retrieval is bypassed, it passes that destination to the vector helper, which can insert vectors there. No destination-collection authorization check is visible in the traced flow.

observations.subject: process_file route
observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file in retrieval.py, included by main.py under the /api/v1/retrieval router prefix; the handler requires form_data and a verified user dependency.

observations.subject: verified caller
observations.claim: The caller is the user object supplied by Depends(get_verified_user); the handler branches on user.role and uses user.id for non-admin file selection.

observations.subject: supplied file_id
observations.claim: The supplied form_data.file_id selects the file. Admin callers fetch by file ID alone; non-admin callers fetch by file ID together with user.id, so the non-admin lookup is directly owner-bound.

observations.subject: file existence and caller branch
observations.claim: Processing proceeds only if the selected file is truthy. Admin role permits lookup without an owner predicate; all other roles use the owner-constrained lookup. A missing or unauthorized non-admin selection reaches the same visible not-found response branch.

observations.subject: destination collection_name
observations.claim: The destination is form_data.collection_name when supplied; otherwise it is derived as file-{file.id}. The supplied collection name is not used in the file-selection guard.

observations.subject: processing and vector write
observations.claim: After file selection, the handler builds documents from supplied content, previously stored vector content, a loader over file.path, or file.data. It updates the selected file's content/status/hash and, when embedding/retrieval is enabled, calls save_docs_to_vector_db with the selected collection_name and metadata containing the selected file.id; that function ultimately inserts vector items into that collection.

observations.subject: shared-file access helper
observations.claim: retrieval.py imports has_access_to_file, but the visible process_file body does not call it. The helper itself supports ownership and several sharing relationships, but its documented use is not evidenced on this path.

observations.subject: same selected file
observations.claim: The input object is the file selected from form_data.file_id. The handler uses that same file.id for document metadata, file-data updates, final metadata/status/hash updates, and the vector-write metadata.

observations.subject: collection versus file
observations.claim: The file identity and collection identity are distinct: file.id identifies the authorized/selected file, while collection_name may be caller-supplied and may name a collection unrelated by source-visible authorization to that file.

observations.subject: output target
observations.claim: The protected input object and file-record effects are the same selected file, but the vector effect targets the separately chosen collection_name. Therefore input-file identity and all output targets are not uniformly the same object.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both scenarios enter the same POST handler and are subject to the admin/non-admin file lookup branch before processing.

observations.subject: caller-owned file
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller whose user.id equals the file's owner identity used by get_file_by_id_and_user_id, the file is selected and processing can continue, subject to the later processing and configuration conditions.

observations.subject: file owned by another user
observations.claim: For a non-admin caller and a file owned by another user, the owner-constrained lookup does not select that file on the visible path, so the handler raises HTTP 404 and does not reach processing or vector insertion. The source does not show a sharing/access-grant exception in this handler.

observations.subject: admin caller
observations.claim: An admin caller is an explicit exception: the handler fetches by file ID without the non-admin owner predicate, so an existing file owned by another user can proceed. This does not establish any destination-collection ownership or authorization.

observations.subject: destination collection
observations.claim: Caller ownership of the file does not imply ownership of form_data.collection_name. The visible process_file path does not check collection ownership or collection access before passing the name to vector operations.

observations.subject: successful owned-file path
observations.claim: When processing succeeds, the selected file record is updated and vector items can be inserted into the supplied collection or the derived file-{file.id} collection, depending on the request and configuration.

observations.subject: content and collection branches
observations.claim: Visible branches are: supplied content takes precedence and deletes the file-{file.id} async vector collection before rebuilding docs; a supplied collection without content first queries file-{file.id} for prior content and otherwise uses file.data; with neither, the handler loads from storage when file.path exists or uses file.data.

observations.subject: bypass configuration
observations.claim: If BYPASS_EMBEDDING_AND_RETRIEVAL is enabled, the handler updates file status/hash and returns success without calling save_docs_to_vector_db; the returned collection_name is None.

observations.subject: vector-write conditions
observations.claim: When bypass is disabled, save_docs_to_vector_db may return early if the destination collection already exists and add is false; add is true only when form_data.collection_name was supplied. Otherwise it generates embeddings and inserts items into the named collection.

observations.subject: duplicate and content limits
observations.claim: The vector helper checks an existing document hash and raises a duplicate-content error when the existing metadata file_id differs; empty post-split documents and invalid splitter configuration also fail before insertion.

observations.subject: failure behavior
observations.claim: Processing exceptions update the selected file status to failed and clear its hash, then return an HTTP 400 for the visible handler-level error path; a missing selected file returns HTTP 404.

observations.subject: authorization limits
observations.claim: The visible authorization limit is file selection by admin role or exact caller ownership lookup for non-admins. No destination collection authorization, collection-owner binding, or invocation of the imported generalized file-access helper is shown in this path.

behavior.explanation: The endpoint binds the caller through Depends(get_verified_user), then authorizes selection of the supplied file_id by role: admins look up any file by ID, while non-admins use a lookup constrained by both file_id and user.id. If a file is selected, the destination is the supplied collection_name or the derived name file-{file.id}. The handler processes content and updates the selected file; unless retrieval is bypassed, it passes that destination to the vector helper, which can insert vectors there. No destination-collection authorization check is visible in the traced flow.

branches.explanation: The caller-bound file can proceed to processing, subject to later conditions.

branches.explanation: The handler raises HTTP 404 before processing or vector insertion.

branches.condition: A file is selected and form_data.collection_name is supplied.
branches.explanation: That caller-supplied name is passed to save_docs_to_vector_db; no collection ownership or access guard is visible before the call.

branches.condition: A file is selected and form_data.collection_name is absent.
branches.explanation: The destination is derived as file-{file.id}; later bypass, collection-existence, processing, and vector conditions still apply.

observations.claim: The entry is POST /process/file on the retrieval router, mounted under /api/v1/retrieval; it receives ProcessFileForm and Depends(get_verified_user).

observations.subject: verified caller

observations.subject: role-specific file selection

observations.subject: file identity versus collection identity
observations.claim: The selected file.id and destination collection_name are distinct identifiers, and collection_name may be caller-supplied.

observations.subject: output targets
observations.claim: File-record effects target the selected file, while vector insertion targets collection_name; vector metadata links the inserted items back to file.id.

observations.subject: ownership scenarios
observations.claim: Both caller-owned and other-user-file scenarios enter the same verified-user endpoint and encounter the admin/non-admin lookup branch first.

observations.subject: non-admin caller-owned file

observations.subject: other user's file

observations.subject: destination collection

observations.subject: successful selected-file path

observations.subject: caller role and ID

observations.subject: processing source and destination

observations.subject: processing and vector conditions
